title: Protocol for the expansion of mouse immune effector cells for in vitro and in vivo studies
protocol: Dilute αCD3 antibodies in 12 mL DPBS to a final concentration of 1 μg/mL.
Dilute αCD28 antibodies in 12 mL DPBS to a final concentration of 5 μg/mL.
Transfer 2 mL of antibody dilution per well onto each well of a 6-well suspension plate.
Wrap the plate in aluminum foil.
Incubate the plate for 8–16 hours at 4°C.
Prepare a 50 mL centrifuge tube with DPBS on ice.
Sacrifice one mouse and disinfect the abdominal skin with 70% ethanol.
Isolate the spleen using sterile instruments.
Open the peritoneum using forceps and scissors.
Expose the spleen by pulling associated white connective tissue with forceps.
Remove unwanted tissue with scissors and transfer the spleen into the 50 mL centrifuge tube.
Place a 100 μm cell strainer in a new 50 mL centrifuge tube.
Mash the spleen with a plunger of a 2 mL syringe while moistening the cell strainer with DPBS.
Fill the tube with DPBS to ensure continuous moistness.
Spin at 400 g for 5 minutes.
Aspirate the supernatant.
Resuspend the red pellet in room-tempered ACK lysis buffer using a 1000 μL pipette.
Use 500 μL ACK lysis buffer per spleen.
Incubate for 2–3 minutes.
Fill the tube with DPBS.
Pass cells through a 40 or 70 μm cell strainer to remove clumps and debris.
Moisten the cell strainer with DPBS before use.
Spin at 400 g for 5 minutes.
Aspirate the supernatant.
Resuspend the pellet in RPMI complete medium.
Count cells with a hemocytometer at a 1:20 dilution.
Aspirate the remaining supernatant from αCD3/CD28-coated 6-well plates.
Wash once with DPBS to remove unbound antibodies.
Seed 5 × 10^6 isolated splenocytes in 5 mL RPMI complete medium per coated well.
Supplement the medium with 50 U/mL IL-2 on day 1.
Harvest cells with a serological pipette on day 2.
Detach cells by pipetting up and down.
Transfer cell suspension into a 50 mL centrifuge tube.
Add 1 mL DPBS to remaining cells.
Detach cells with a 1000 μL pipette.
Combine cell fractions.
Spin the cell suspension at 400 g for 5 min.
Resuspend in appropriate volume of RPMI complete medium.
Count the cells.
Reseed cells at a concentration of 1 × 10^6 cells/mL with 0.5 mL/cm².
Supplement the medium with 50 U/mL IL-2.
Count cell numbers every 1–2 days.
Expand with additional RPMI complete medium to maintain a concentration of 1 × 10^6 cells/mL with 0.5 mL/cm².
Supplement additional medium with 50 U/mL IL-2.
Spin splenocytes in recommended medium at 400 g for 5 min and aspirate the supernatant.
Resuspend the splenocyte pellet at 1 × 10^6 cells/mL in recommended medium.
Follow instructions of the EasySep Mouse NK Cell Isolation Kit.
Spin the isolated NK cell suspension at 400 g for 5 min and aspirate the supernatant.
Resuspend the pellet in 1 mL medium to get ∼1–2 × 10^6 cells/mL.
Count cells with a hemocytometer at a 1:5 dilution.
Seed NK cells at a concentration of 0.5 × 10^6 cells/mL in 800 μL MEMα complete medium/well on a 24-well suspension plate.
Supplement medium with 150 ng/mL IL-15.
On day 3, count the cell suspension with a hemocytometer and expand with additional MEMα complete medium to reach 0.4 × 10^6 cells/mL with 0.25 mL/cm².
Supplement additional medium with 150 ng/mL IL-15.
Count cell numbers every 2 days.
Expand culture with additional MEMα complete medium to maintain a concentration of 0.4 × 10^6 cells/mL using 0.25 mL/cm².
Supplement the added medium with 150 ng/mL IL-15.
Maintain NK cells on uncoated suspension plates/flasks.
Isolate bone marrow cells from both femora and tibiae of one C57BL/6 mouse.
Prepare a 50 mL centrifuge tube with DPBS on ice.
Sacrifice one mouse.
Disinfect the skin at the legs and abdomen with 70% ethanol.
Make an incision at the top of each hind leg.
Pull the skin down towards the foot to expose the muscle.
Cut the cartilage between femur and tibia.
Free the hind legs from muscles using scissors.
Perform amputation, twisting carefully to isolate the femur without breaking bones.
Use a paper tissue sprayed with 70% ethanol to remove remaining muscle tissue from the bones.
Spray the bones with 70% ethanol to disinfect.
Wait 30 seconds after spraying the bones.
Transfer the bones into a 50 mL centrifuge tube filled with DPBS for transport.
Place the bones on a petri dish under a sterile working bench.
Remove remaining connective tissue with forceps and scalpel by scratching.
Cut the cartilage at both sides of the bone to allow excess to the bone marrow.
Attach a 25G needle to a 10 mL syringe.
Flush the bone cavity with DMEM/F12 complete medium into a 50 mL centrifuge tube until the bone cavity appears white.
Spin at 400 g for 5 minutes and aspirate the supernatant.
Resuspend the red pellet in room-tempered ACK lysis buffer using a 1000 μL pipette.
Incubate for 2–3 minutes and fill with DPBS.
Pass cells through a 40 μm or 70 μm cell strainer to remove clumps and debris.
Moisten the cell strainer with DPBS or medium before use.
Spin the cell suspension at 400 g for 5 minutes.
Aspirate the supernatant.
Resuspend the pellet in DMEM/F12 complete medium to achieve a concentration of ∼4–6 × 10^6 cells/mL.
Count bone marrow cells using an automated cell counter or hemocytometer at a 1:10 dilution.
Seed bone marrow cells diluted to 0.2–0.25 × 10^6 cells/mL in DMEM/F-12 complete medium supplemented with 20% L929 conditioned medium.
Add 12 mL of cell suspension per non-adherent 10 cm Petri dish.
Perform a partial medium change on day 3 and day 5 by carefully tilting the plate and gently removing 7 mL medium using a serological pipette.
Replace removed medium with fresh DMEM/F-12 complete medium supplemented with 20% L929 conditioned medium to reach a total volume of 12 mL.
Aspirate the medium from the plate on day 3 carefully.
Wash the cells once with 5 mL DPBS.
Add 5 mL of cold DPBS with 2.5 mM EDTA per plate.
Incubate for 10–20 min on ice or at 4°C in the fridge.
Gently resuspend detaching cells with a serological pipette and collect them in a 50 mL centrifuge tube.
Add additional DPBS + 2.5 mM EDTA to collect remaining cells.
Centrifuge at 350 g for 5 min and discard the supernatant.
Flick the pellet and resuspend the cells in required buffer or medium.
